evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError is the base class, and NotFoundError and ConflictError extend it. project.ts, user.ts, task.ts and task-status.ts all use this hierarchy consistently.
src/domain/task-status.ts: TaskStatusValue and TaskStatus.values are the only place the allowed statuses are defined, and TaskStatus.create validates against them.
src/domain/task.ts: Task.markDone() checks this.status.isDone() and sets the status through TaskStatus.create('done'), so it uses the value object instead of raw strings.
src/domain/repositories.ts: UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository are typed against the domain entities, and TaskFilters.status reuses TaskStatusValue from task-status.ts.
src/domain/project.ts and src/domain/user.ts: each constructor checks only its own entity's required fields and throws DomainError.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the task-management domain model. That includes the entities (Project, User, Task), the TaskStatus value object, the domain error hierarchy, and the repository ports. Every file uses the module's own abstractions the same way. Validation failures throw DomainError or one of its subclasses from errors.ts. Task holds a TaskStatus and delegates the done check to TaskStatus.isDone() instead of comparing raw strings. All repository ports are typed against the domain entities. The set of allowed statuses lives only in task-status.ts, and TaskFilters reuses that type instead of redefining it. Project and User have similar required-field checks, but each checks its own entity's invariant, so this is not one rule duplicated. A small inconsistency: Task.markDone calls TaskStatus.create('done') instead of a dedicated factory like todo(). It still goes through the value object's validation, so this is not a bypass. No file splits into an unrelated concern.
